requirements.quote:
Endpoints maintain separate read and write secrets for packet
   protection.
requirements.required_behavior: Maintain distinct read and write traffic secrets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Represent read and write packet protection with one undifferentiated traffic secret.
requirements.why_checkable: Endpoint key state and derivation events can be inspected to verify separate read-direction and write-direction secrets.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint initiates a key update by updating its
   packet protection write secret
requirements.condition: When an endpoint initiates a key update
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Initiate the update while leaving the write secret unchanged.
requirements.why_checkable: The key-update transition can be instrumented to compare the write secret before and after initiation.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint initiates a key update by updating its
   packet protection write secret and using that to protect new packets.
requirements.condition: After an endpoint updates its packet-protection write secret
requirements.required_behavior: Use the updated write secret's protection material for newly sent packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Continue protecting new packets with the superseded write secret as the current key phase.
requirements.why_checkable: Packets sent after the update can be tested against old and new key material to identify which write secret protects them.

requirements.quote:
The endpoint creates a new write secret from the existing write
   secret as performed in Section 7.2 of [TLS13].  This uses the KDF
   function provided by TLS with a label of "quic ku".
requirements.condition: When deriving the next packet-protection write secret
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the TLS-provided KDF to the existing write secret using the label "quic ku" as specified by TLS 1.3 key update derivation.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Derive the next write secret from an unrelated secret or with a different label.
requirements.why_checkable: Given a known current write secret and negotiated KDF, the next secret can be compared with a reference derivation using the exact label.

requirements.quote:
The
   corresponding key and IV are created from that secret as defined in
   Section 5.1.
requirements.condition: After deriving a new write secret for a key update
requirements.required_behavior: Derive the corresponding packet-protection key from the new secret according to Section 5.1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse the old packet-protection key as the updated phase's key.
requirements.why_checkable: The installed key can be compared with the Section 5.1 derivation output for the new secret.

requirements.quote:
The
   corresponding key and IV are created from that secret as defined in
   Section 5.1.
requirements.condition: After deriving a new write secret for a key update
requirements.required_behavior: Derive the corresponding packet-protection IV from the new secret according to Section 5.1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reuse the old packet-protection IV as the updated phase's IV.
requirements.why_checkable: The installed IV can be compared with the Section 5.1 derivation output for the new secret.

requirements.quote: The header protection key is not updated.
requirements.condition: When updating packet-protection keys for a new key phase
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the header protection key unchanged.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Derive or install a new header protection key as part of the key update.
requirements.why_checkable: The header protection key before and after a key-update transition can be compared for equality.

requirements.condition: When updating write keys with TLS 1.3
requirements.required_behavior: Compute secret_<n+1> with HKDF-Expand-Label(secret_<n>, "quic ku", empty context, Hash.length).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a nonempty context or an output length other than Hash.length for this expansion.
requirements.why_checkable: Known secret_<n> test vectors can be expanded with the exact parameters and compared byte-for-byte with secret_<n+1>.

requirements.quote: The endpoint toggles the value of the Key Phase bit
requirements.condition: When an endpoint activates updated write keys
requirements.required_behavior: Toggle the Key Phase bit from its value in the preceding key phase.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Leave the Key Phase bit unchanged for packets in the newly activated phase.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet headers immediately before and after the write-key update can be decoded to compare Key Phase bit values.

requirements.quote:
uses the
   updated key and IV to protect all subsequent packets.
requirements.condition: After activating a new write-key phase
requirements.required_behavior: Protect every subsequently sent packet with the updated key and IV until another permitted update.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Protect a subsequent current-phase packet with the superseded key or IV.
requirements.why_checkable: Each packet after activation can be tested against the old and updated key/IV pair.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST NOT initiate a key update prior to having confirmed
   the handshake (Section 4.1.2).
requirements.condition: Before the endpoint has confirmed the handshake
requirements.why_checkable: A state-machine test can attempt or observe a key update before the handshake-confirmed event and assert that no update occurs.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST NOT initiate a
   subsequent key update unless it has received an acknowledgment for a
   packet that was sent protected with keys from the current key phase.
requirements.condition: After one key update and before initiating the next key update
requirements.required_behavior: Wait until receiving an acknowledgment for a packet protected with keys from the current key phase.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Initiate the subsequent key update before receiving such an acknowledgment.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can withhold acknowledgments for current-phase packets and verify that another key-update transition does not occur.

requirements.quote:
Keys of packets other than the 1-RTT packets are never
      |  updated
requirements.condition: For packet-protection keys belonging to packet types other than 1-RTT
requirements.required_behavior: Keep those keys unchanged for their lifetime.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply the QUIC key-update mechanism to those keys.
requirements.why_checkable: Key state for Initial, 0-RTT, and Handshake packet types can be compared across 1-RTT key updates.

requirements.quote:
their keys are derived solely from the TLS handshake
      |  state.
requirements.condition: When deriving keys for packet types other than 1-RTT
requirements.required_behavior: Derive those keys solely from TLS handshake state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Derive them from the 1-RTT key-update chain.
requirements.why_checkable: Key provenance can be traced to handshake secrets and checked for independence from later 1-RTT update secrets.

requirements.quote:
The endpoint that initiates a key update also updates the keys that
   it uses for receiving packets.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint initiates a write-side key update
requirements.required_behavior: Also update the packet-protection keys used for receiving packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Leave receive-side keys unavailable for the peer's corresponding update.
requirements.why_checkable: The initiator's receive-key state can be observed before and after its write-side update and exercised with a peer packet in the new phase.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST retain old keys until it has successfully
   unprotected a packet sent using the new keys.
requirements.condition: After installing new keys but before successfully unprotecting a packet sent with them
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Discard the old keys before successfully unprotecting a packet with the new keys.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can delay delivery of a valid new-key packet and inspect whether old-key packets remain decryptable until that success event.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint SHOULD
   retain old keys for some time after unprotecting a packet sent using
   the new keys.
requirements.condition: After successfully unprotecting a packet sent using the new keys
requirements.required_behavior: Continue retaining the old keys for a nonzero period to accommodate delayed packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Discard the old keys immediately without a justified exception to the SHOULD.
requirements.why_checkable: A delayed old-key packet can be delivered shortly after the first successful new-key packet to determine whether an overlap retention period exists.
